M2: Energy Access and Inclusive Energy Services
Chapter 2 Overview

Despite decades of progress, deep inequalities continue to define the global energy access landscape.

This chapter explores the current status, emerging trends, and systemic barriers that prevent billions of people from accessing reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy.

It begins by mapping the geography of energy access gaps—across regions, rural and urban divides, fragile settings, and informal settlements—and zooms into the layered realities that shape energy poverty, from inadequate infrastructure to socio-economic exclusion.

The chapter goes beyond electricity, highlighting the urgent need for clean cooking 💬️, heating, and cooling, especially in contexts where energy deprivation intersects with gender, climate vulnerability, and displacement.

Drawing on the latest data, case studies, and regional examples, it challenges learners to understand energy access not just as a technical issue, but as a deeply structural one—entwined with public health, economic opportunity, and climate resilience.

It closes by unpacking the institutional, financial, and governance-related barriers that block progress toward universal access and calls for more inclusive, resilient, and context-sensitive solutions.
